findings.text: The index-currency predicate (the length check at 1089 and the per-file stamp loop at 1091-1093) has no assertion anywhere: the gate's fixture writes every ledger run file before its warm-up read_records call and never mutates the ledger afterwards, so deleting the whole validation block leaves the gate green while run_ids would serve a stale index's membership after a run file is added or rewritten in place. Exercise it by adding a run file after the warm-up and asserting the next run_ids includes it.

The stale-index refresh branch introduced by the final commit (run_ids calls load(..., headers_only=True) when the index exists but is not current) is never entered by the gate, because the warm-up read leaves the index current for the whole test. A regression that dropped the refresh and fell straight back to _load_aggregate would still pass, since the one-pass count assertion is satisfied by the fresh-index path alone.

_indexed_run_ids repeats the read-only index prologue owned by _last_good_index_data (the connection and aggregate-stamp comparison at 1070-1077 against 1475-1482) and a variant of the membership union owned by _index_payload (1082-1083 against 1406-1408), extending neither. The two unions already differ on a run file whose record the index could not decode: _indexed_run_ids counts it by name while _index_payload's headers_only projection drops it, so the two expressions of one question can drift. The capability it needs, validated membership without decoding, genuinely has no owner yet, which is why this is recorded rather than treated as a fork.

The baseline_suite and after_suite command values carry a placeholder, "<eight importer test files>", which the manifest contract refuses because the arm cannot be re-run from it. The literal commands are recoverable from the two logs' own # command: headers and agree with the manifest's claim, so both arms are sound; the recorded field is what needs repairing.
